facts.claim: 开篇第一条就把年代钉在十三世纪中美洲羊皮纸，用 Incan paper 谐音 ink and paper 起梗
facts.quote: I was recently offered a contract to sign on some thirteenth-century Central American parchment.

facts.claim: 年代顺序并不严格递进，而是按朝代/年代自由串烧：罗马段用两根手指当五杯啤酒，靠手势与数字的错位出笑点
facts.quote: A Roman walks into a bar, holds up two fingers and says, ‘Five beers please.’

facts.claim: 历史人物段拿亚历山大大帝的军队开涮，把 sleeves 说成 sleevies 与 arm 双关
facts.quote: Where did Alexander the Great keep his armies? Up his sleevies.

facts.claim: 近世/思想史段用马克思与“财产”梗：proper tea 谐音 property，接 all property is theft 的旧口号
facts.quote: Why did Karl Marx drink coffee? Because all proper tea is theft.

facts.claim: 美国内战段把“站在历史错误一边”落到李将军身上，用 General Lee 谐音 generally
facts.quote: Did the Confederate army in the American Civil War know they were on the wrong side of history? Not General Lee.

facts.claim: 恐龙与博物馆段是一则长故事：守卫把“七千一百万零四年半”说成精确到月，靠入职时间加总
facts.quote: Without a moment’s hesitation, the guard replies, ‘It’s 71,000,004 years and six months.’

facts.claim: 中世纪段落在亚瑟王的圆桌上做文章，把“最圆的骑士”拗成圆周谐音 Sir Cumference
facts.quote: Who was the roundest knight at King Arthur’s table? Sir Cumference.

facts.claim: 章末并入 Pirates! 小节（标题重复两次），笑话从年代梗改成海盗口音的字母/同音梗
facts.quote: What’s actually a pirate’s favourite letter? ‘P’: without it, a pirate’s irate!

relations.relation: 两条都把数字当笑点：一条把两指读成五杯，一条把 constantine 拆出 teen，靠数字与词的错位
relations.quote: What ancient Roman leader never turned twenty? Emperor Constant-teen.

relations.relation: 都靠把专名硬拗成谐音：armies 藏进 sleeves，圆桌骑士变成圆周，机制是“先有谐音再补故事”
relations.quote: Who was the roundest knight at King Arthur’s table? Sir Cumference.

relations.pair: 历史年代段 / Pirates! 小节
relations.relation: 并入的海盗小节不再按年代排列，笑点全在海盗口音的同音词（buck an ear、irate），与前面历史梗的机制不同
relations.quote: What do pirates charge for piercings? A buck an ear.

relations.relation: 同一条“考古学家事业成废墟”的笑话在本章出现两次，一次作问句一次作定义，是全章唯一重复的梗
relations.quote: What is an archaeologist? Someone whose career is in ruins.

numbers.meaning: 博物馆守卫报出的恐龙骨龄，精确到月，由“入职时七千万年”加“四年半”凑出
numbers.quote: the guard replies, ‘It’s 71,000,004 years and six months.’

numbers.value: 71 million years old / four and a half years ago
numbers.meaning: 守卫算法的两个加数：骨头入职时七千万岁，他本人在此工作了四年半
numbers.quote: They were 71 million years old when I started working here, and that was four and a half years ago.

numbers.meaning: 一则古希腊油渍笑话把年代具体到三千年，用“古”本身当笑点
numbers.quote: I saw a 3,000-year-old oil stain. It was from Ancient Greece.

numbers.meaning: 海盗笑话里的年龄：七十九岁生日一年后，他说 Aye, matey（谐音 eighty）
numbers.quote: What did the pirate say a year after his seventy-ninth birthday? ‘Aye, matey!’
